1.explanation: The bug arises because the decorator rule ({ className: 'meta', begin: /^[\t ]*@/, end: /$/ }) matches from the '@' at the start of the line all the way through the inline comment, preventing hljs.HASH_COMMENT_MODE from ever matching the comment text. To fix it you must adjust the decorator meta rule (for example by excluding '#' in its end pattern or adding hljs.HASH_COMMENT_MODE to its contains) so that the comment portion is handed off to the comment highlighter rather than swallowed as metadata.
1.bug_scenario: In Python code with a decorator and an inline comment (e.g. @pytest.mark.asyncio  # note use of pytest-asyncio marker), the entire line is being highlighted as metadata (hljs-meta) instead of splitting out the ‘# …’ as a comment (hljs-comment). The decorator rule in the highlighter is consuming the comment portion before the comment mode can match.

2.explanation: The offending rule lives in python.js: the anonymous export default function defines a ‘meta’ mode with begin:/^[\t ]*@/ and end:/$/. That pattern eats the entire decorator line—including any ‘#’ comments—so the inline comment never matches hljs.HASH_COMMENT_MODE. To fix the bug, this meta rule must be adjusted (for example, end before a ‘#’ or exclude comment tokens) so that the comment segment can be recognized and highlighted as hljs-comment.
2.bug_scenario: In Python code blocks, lines starting with a decorator (the “@…” syntax) that also include an inline comment ("# …") are being entirely marked with the hljs-meta class. As a result, the comment portion never receives the hljs-comment styling (greyed-out text) and instead is treated as part of the decorator. In the screenshot you can see “# note use of pytest-asyncio marker” remains blue (meta) instead of grey.
